items.title: One UI 9.5 could make booking an Uber part of your Now Brief routine
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Samsung is working on proactive ride-booking suggestions for Now Brief and Now Nudge in One UI 9.5. 
 Your Galaxy phone could suggest booking a ride through Gemini based on your upcoming appointments and departure times. 
 The underlying code references Uber, Lyft, Kakao T, and DiDi as supported ride-hailing apps. 

Say you have a dinner reservation at 7 PM. Samsung’s Now Brief can already remind you about it, show you the restaurant’s location, and let you know when it’s time to leave. But getting there is still your responsibility. You could open Uber or even ask Gemini to book a ride for you. With One UI 9.5 , Samsung appears to be working on connecting those dots so that your Galaxy phone can offer to arrange a ride before you even ask.

Earlier this week, we learned that Samsung is developing a Daily Briefing feature for Now Brief that can automatically generate reminders using information from other apps. Now, an APK teardown by SammyGuru has revealed how Samsung could turn some of those reminders into actionable suggestions.
items.t: One UI 9.5 could make booking an Uber part of your Now Brief routine

items.title: Samsung’s Origin laptops will plug into the Galaxy ecosystem, and One UI is laying the foundation
items.summary:
Credit: Zac Kew-Denniss / Android Authority 

TL;DR 

Code in One UI 9.5 Beta 1 reveals that Samsung is laying the groundwork in its Android apps to plug its upcoming origin14 and origin16 (likely the XE940 and XE960) laptops into the Galaxy ecosystem. 
 Supported continuity tools could include Call & text on other devices, Multi Control, Storage Share, Galaxy Buds auto-switching, phone-as-a-webcam sharing, instant hotspot sharing with Windows PCs, and offline Find My Mobile tracking. 
 Smart View could also gain Mirror and Extend display modes alongside Second Screen support, while Galaxy AI tools like Now Brief and Now Nudge could get dedicated laptop layouts. 

Samsung’s upcoming Android laptops will plug straight into the Galaxy ecosystem, according to code in the One UI 9.5 Beta 1. We found the laptops’ codenames, origin14 and origin16, earlier today, along with their dedicated One UI laptop interface with Circle to Search , and the same build lays the foundation for adapting most of Samsung’s connected-device features to them.

APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

Samsung already offers most of these connected-device features on its Windows-based Galaxy Book laptops, through Windows apps. The new strings below are different, though. They sit in the Android versions of Samsung’s apps and refer to “this laptop,” meaning One UI itself is running on the laptop. Several of these apps, including Smart View and Find My Mobile, will also check whether they’re running on a “desktop” class device, the same check…
items.t: Samsung’s Origin laptops will plug into the Galaxy ecosystem, and One UI is laying the foundation

items.title: OpenAI’s first smartphone could launch in 2027 with help from iPhone manufacturer
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Foxconn subsidiary FIH Mobile has reportedly secured an order to assemble OpenAI’s first smartphone. 
 Several other Apple suppliers are reportedly involved, with the phone potentially launching in late 2027 or 2028. 
 The device is expected to feature a custom MediaTek chip and an AI-first user experience, but its operating system remains unknown. 

For a company whose most recognizable product lives inside an app on your phone, OpenAI appears increasingly interested in making the phone itself. We first heard about its smartphone ambitions in April , and a new report from China suggests the project is making headway with familiar names from Apple’s supply chain.

Citing supply chain sources, Chinese publication Securities Times (via Abhishek Yadav on X ) reports that Foxconn subsidiary FIH Mobile has secured an order to assemble OpenAI’s smartphone. Foxconn is already one of Apple’s biggest iPhone manufacturing partners, meaning the company could soon have another major smartphone client with roots in Cupertino.
items.t: OpenAI’s first smartphone could launch in 2027 with help from iPhone manufacturer

items.title: One UI 9.5 beta quietly kills Audio Brief and Moments in Now Brief
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Samsung has removed Audio Brief and Moments from the Now Brief tool with the latest One UI 9.5 beta. 
 The company’s official One UI 9.5 changelog confirms the removal of these Now Brief features. 
 When features are removed this way, it typically means they’re either underused or too resource-intensive to maintain, though Samsung hasn’t explained why it removed Audio Brief and Moments. 

While we’re still learning about the new features in the One UI 9.5 beta for the Galaxy S26 series, the official changelog also mentions a couple of omissions that have largely gone under the radar. We’ve previously learned that Now Brief could gain a new tool called Daily Brief with One UI 9.5 , but it’s now confirmed that Now Brief will lose Moments and Audio Brief.

For those unfamiliar with these two features, Audio Brief taps into Galaxy AI to summarize your Now Brief cards and read them out, while Moments provides a daily recap of the best photos and videos you’ve captured that day. According to the official One UI 9.5 changelog, these two features have been removed.

items.title: Exclusive: Samsung’s upcoming 14-inch and 16-inch Android laptops are codenamed ‘Origin’
items.summary:
Samsung Galaxy Book 6 Ultra 

Credit: Lanh Nguyen / Android Authority 

TL;DR 

Code in Samsung’s One UI 9.5 Beta 1 reveals two upcoming Wi-Fi-only Android laptops codenamed “origin14wifi” and “origin16wifi” (likely model numbers XE940 and XE960), likely featuring 14-inch and 16-inch clamshell designs. 
 Both models appear to run on Qualcomm’s 12-core Snapdragon X Elite (X1E-80-100) chip, with the 16-inch XE960 showing signs of touchscreen support. 
 Despite Google’s “Googlebook” branding used by partners like Dell and HP, Samsung’s code makes no mention of Googlebook or “Aluminium,” referring to the devices simply as “laptops.” 

Samsung’s Android laptops are codenamed “Origin,” according to code in the One UI 9.5 beta. The beta, which I installed on my Galaxy S26 Ultra, references two devices called “origin14wifi” and “origin16wifi,” which point to Wi-Fi-only laptops with 14-inch and 16-inch screens. The same build names Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X Elite chip and two laptop model numbers, XE940 and XE960.

APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

Samsung’s Android laptop plans have been an open secret for most of this year. Back in April, it was reported that Samsung was building Galaxy Book laptops running Android 17 and One UI 9 . Samsung was missing from Google’s first Googlebook partners , but Google VP John Maletis told Chrome Unboxed in May that “you should expect more logos over time.” A Samsung laptop running Android 17, the XE940XSA, appeared on Geekbench in October, as spotted by Abhishek Yadav on X back then.
items.t: Exclusive: Samsung’s upcoming 14-inch and 16-inch Android laptops are codenamed ‘Origin’

items.title: This free app brought Samsung’s best automation feature to my Google Pixel

I’ve used this nifty automation tool for smoothing out more than a few wrinkles in my digital life, from switching Android Auto devices with just a tap of an NFC chip to triggering various features before I leave the house. items.title: A mystery Motorola ‘Raptor27’ phone just cleared the FCC, and it looks like a 2027 Razr flip
items.summary:
TL;DR 

An unannounced Motorola phone with the model number XT2765-1 has received FCC certification. 
 The device, previously linked to the Raptor27 codename, follows a model numbering pattern similar to recent Motorola Razr foldables. 
 FCC documents reveal support for 5G, Wi-Fi 6E, Bluetooth, NFC, and wireless charging, but the phone’s commercial name remains unknown. 

Motorola’s foldable family is starting to look a lot bigger than it did a year ago. The arrival of the Razr Fold gave the company something to offer beyond its familiar flip phones, and we’ve already seen evidence of a smaller, wider foldable called the Razr Flex 2027 . But Motorola hasn’t forgotten the form factor that brought the Razr name back to life, and a new regulatory filing could offer our first glimpse of its next-generation flip phone plans.

We’ve discovered a yet-to-be-announced Motorola smartphone with the model number XT2765-1 that cleared the US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) on November 13. While the listing doesn’t reveal the phone’s commercial name, one of the accompanying test reports explicitly identifies it as a folding phone and details testing in both open and closed positions. Digging into Motorola’s recent model numbers also offers some interesting clues about where it could fit into the company’s foldable lineup.
items.t: A mystery Motorola ‘Raptor27’ phone just cleared the FCC, and it looks like a 2027 Razr flip
